title: Attribution Guard QA
eyebrow: QA · pull request #320, which fixes #315: the attribution guard misses gh api and curl

short.lead: The fix is built and open as pull request #320. The credit check now refuses a Claude credit on every route an agent writes to GitHub, recognises the footer GitHub appends, and reads the body back after each write. Of the 8 cases from #315, main let 7 through; this branch refuses all 8. The test suite has no new failures. One thing only you can test: a real cloud session.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was checked and how.
items: I ran the guard on the 8 cases from #315: two gh pr create bodies, five gh api routes and curl. All 8 were refused. A plain gh api read still goes through.
The read-back works against live GitHub
Run on #315, which has the footer GitHub really appended, the hook warned that GitHub had added a Claude credit. Run on #316, the hook said no Claude credit was on it.
verify.py: 4 of 847 checks fail, the same 4 that fail on a clean copy of main. tools/verify_tools.py: all 47 pass.
Open one item from a cloud session

Cloud sessions install the plugin from main, so this test runs after #320 merges. Start a cloud session, ask it to open a test issue with gh api, then compare the credit-check message the agent shows with the issue on GitHub.
Run it, then pass or fail QA.

changes: gh api writes and curl to the GitHub API are checked.
git commit, gh pr and gh issue only.
Also gh api writes to pulls, issues and comments, curl to api.github.com, and bodies in -F body=@file or --input files.
The appended "Generated by Claude Code" footer is caught.
6 patterns; the footer passed even on gh pr create.
8 patterns; the footer is refused on every route.
A PostToolUse hook on Bash reads the body back once after a write.
No read-back; a reply could claim the credit was clean.
The agent is told whether a Claude credit is on the item, or that it could not check.
The rule says the badge and footer are reported, not promised away.

unverified: The read-back has not run inside a real cloud session, only against live GitHub from this machine
With gh api -f body=@file, gh sends the text "@file" as the body instead of the file's contents, so the check reads the command text itself. Only -F and --input read the file.

wrapup.summary: The credit check covers every GitHub write route and reads the body back. Pull request #320 waits for your QA.
wrapup.changing: hook.py, hooks.json, verify.py, the rule text, guards.md and the version.
wrapup.next: On your go-ahead I merge #320 to main; you then run the cloud-session test. On a fail I fix it on a new branch.
